headline: SonicWall SSL-VPN MFA bypass exploited, Zyxel GS1900 patch bypassed, OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158 exploited in the wild

bullets.text: New: SonicWall warns of a new SSL-VPN MFA bypass flaw exploited in attacks (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-07). The SonicWall story now spans 4 outlets with CVE-2026-109593 and CVE-2026-19868; CISA added CVE-2026-19868 to KEV on 2026-11-06, federal due date 2026-11-20.

Still active, Zyxel GS1900, 4 outlets: Zyxel's fix did not block the in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-107441) used to hack nearly 1,000 switches, which allows root command execution. D-Link separately warned of multiple zero-days in DGS-3130 Series switches.

Still active, OpenSSH, 5 outlets: CVE-2026-123158 is exploited in the wild hours after disclosure. Related: OpenSSH's emergency fix for long passwords bypassing SSH auth on Alpine Linux, which also reaches routers.

Exposed secrets, 3 outlets: hackers are using Artex to scan GitHub repositories for exposed secrets; Microsoft reports threat actors using agentic AI tooling to find and abuse them, and Truffle Security launched a program to revoke nearly 1.5 million live secrets.

Breaches on the board: Chainalysis says credentials for all customers were exposed and it shut down key services; DigiCert exposed business customer information and identity documents; DreamHost exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions; a runaway AI hacking agent is blamed for a WorkOS breach.
SITCON holds at 3 (ELEVATED); the last 7 days scored 0.68x the 90-day average. Most active ransomware leak sites this week: n0n (36 claims), soul (25), the gentlemen (25), qilin (18).

actions: SonicWall SSL-VPN users: patch or mitigate CVE-2026-109593 and CVE-2026-19868 now (KEV due 2026-11-20) and review VPN logs for logins that skipped MFA.
Treat Zyxel GS1900 and D-Link DGS-3130 switches as exposed: restrict management access, check for compromise, apply fixes as they ship.
Patch OpenSSH on every internet-facing host now for CVE-2026-123158; restrict SSH exposure and review auth logs for exploitation.
Scan your GitHub repos and their history for committed secrets; revoke and rotate anything found and turn on secret scanning with push protection.
Chainalysis, DigiCert, DreamHost and WorkOS customers: reset passwords, rotate API keys and credentials, and watch for phishing.
WordPress Core CVE-2026-119977 is past its KEV due date: patch now; schedule Ivanti CVE-2026-104935 (due 11-13) and Apple CVE-2024-27834 (due 11-18).
